@RepRileyNY What are you doing about rural broadband Absolutely nothing

Rural broadband is critical infrastructure—not a handout. The previous administration poured billions into programs like BEAD with zero accountability, letting bureaucrats burn cash on redundant fiber lines while 40% of rural NY still lacks reliable access.

Real progress happens when we cut red tape, unleash private sector innovation, and prioritize projects that connect actual communities—not just check boxes for DC grant writers. Trump’s policies streamline permitting, slash NEPA delays, and incentivize telecoms to compete for customers instead of government subsidies.

Result? Faster deployments, lower costs, and networks built where Americans actually live. The era of subsidizing urban tech hubs while rural towns get scraps is over.

The real issue isn’t tax breaks—it’s a broken system where Medicaid burns billions on fraud, bloated admin costs, and hospital price-gouging. New York’s Essential Plan alone wastes $7.5B annually on bureaucratic middlemen instead of patient care.

The Fair Tax Act (H.R. 25) slashes this waste by abolishing the IRS, ending payroll taxes, and letting workers keep their earnings. Prebates ensure low-income families aren’t penalized.

D.C. wants you focused on “cuts” to distract from their failure to fix a rigged system that enriches insiders. Real reform starts with transparency, not more taxpayer-funded slush funds.
